question: Which insect spreads the malaria parasite to humans?

options.A: Housefly
options.B: Female Anopheles mosquito
options.C: Tsetse fly
options.D: Male Culex mosquito

explanation: Spot on! Malaria is transmitted specifically when an infected female Anopheles mosquito bites looking for a blood meal. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T3#GNS214_U1_T3_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of monitoring and evaluation in maternal health programs?

options.A: To punish nurses who make mistakes during night shifts
options.B: To track progress, spot system weaknesses, and guide proper resource use
options.C: To reduce the number of women attending antenatal care
options.D: To increase the cost of medications in government clinics

explanation: Monitoring and evaluation provide data that shows what is working and where urgent improvements are needed in the healthcare system. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T44#GNS214_U1_T44_h8)

question: What is an important action to take if a patient tests negative while still within a recent window period?

options.A: Inform the client's employer about their negative status
options.B: Prescribe antiretroviral therapy for lifelong daily use
options.C: Assume the client is fully immune to future HIV exposure
options.D: Schedule a follow-up test after the window period closes

explanation: You got it! Because recent exposure might not show up yet, they need a repeat test later to be 100% sure of their status. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T10#GNS216_U6_T10_h5)

question: What do we call computer hardware?

options.A: The invisible programs and operating instructions
options.B: The secret password protection protocols for patient files
options.C: The physical, touchable parts of the computer system
options.D: The wireless network signals inside a hospital ward

explanation: Think of hardware as anything you can physically touch, like the monitor, keyboard, or mouse at the nursing station. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T5#GNS113_U1_T5_h2)

question: Which of these is a very common field challenge when running community health programs?

options.A: Immediate willingness of all community members to participate
options.B: The complete absence of any administrative or staffing duties
options.C: Transport breakdowns and logistical delays reaching remote areas
options.D: Excessive funding that exceeds what the clinic can possibly spend

explanation: Bad roads, broken vehicles, and travel delays are classic hurdles every community health nurse learns to navigate. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T20#GNS225_U2_T20_h7)

question: Which of these is a realistic, patient-centered nutrition goal?

options.A: Walking for twenty minutes after lunch four days a week
options.B: Losing twenty kilograms by the end of this month
options.C: Eating a much healthier diet starting immediately
options.D: Eliminating all food cravings within forty-eight hours

explanation: Brilliant! This goal is specific, achievable, and easy to measure. Small, steady steps lead to big wins. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T004#GNS227_U7_T004_h3)

question: How does palliative fatigue differ from normal everyday tiredness?

options.A: It only occurs during the first few hours of the morning
options.B: It can always be cured by eating a high-protein meal
options.C: It is caused strictly by a lack of physical exercise
options.D: It does not improve with rest or a good night's sleep

explanation: Palliative fatigue is a deep, systemic exhaustion rooted in the underlying disease process rather than simple lack of sleep. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T15#GNS321_U4_T15_h5)

question: What is the most important human resource needed to keep a healthcare system running?

options.A: Modern commercial advertising agencies
options.B: Trained doctors, nurses, and midwives
options.C: Private transport and logistics companies
options.D: International pharmaceutical investors

explanation: Too easy! Skilled clinical staff like nurses and doctors are the heartbeat of any hospital; without them, patient care just cannot happen. [learn more](GST322_U1_T3#GST322_U1_T3_h3)

question: A newly registered pregnant woman is diagnosed with HIV at her first clinic visit. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Advise her to terminate the pregnancy to protect her health.
options.B: Start her on lifelong antiretroviral therapy immediately.
options.C: Wait until her second trimester before prescribing any medications.
options.D: Delay treatment until her CD4 cell count drops below 200.

explanation: Current guidelines recommend prompt initiation of ART for all pregnant women living with HIV, regardless of clinical stage or CD4 count. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h4)

question: As a nurse, which non-clinical duty do you often perform in financed health systems?

options.A: Managing the national treasury accounts
options.B: Explaining insurance coverage and benefits to patients
options.C: Collecting taxes from local business owners
options.D: Setting the annual interest rates for community loans

explanation: Nurses are great educators! You will often help bridge the gap by explaining complex health programs in plain language patients can easily understand. [learn more](GST322_U4_T4#GST322_U4_T4_h5)

question: What happens if a nurse manager ignores a small workplace disagreement?

options.A: It will automatically resolve itself over time.
options.B: It can grow into a major crisis that threatens patient safety.
options.C: It will improve overall staff productivity.
options.D: It will make doctors respect nurses more.

explanation: Unresolved issues fester and ruin teamwork, which can sadly put patient care in danger. Good to know! [learn more](GST321_U5_T3#GST321_U5_T3_h7)

question: A family wants to eat healthily on a modest budget in Nigeria. Which purchasing approach is best?

options.A: Purchasing only imported cereals and canned soups
options.B: Buying expensive pre-packaged meals from supermarkets
options.C: Avoiding local open markets entirely
options.D: Buying local whole foods like beans, vegetables, and tubers

explanation: Local whole foods provide essential nutrients affordably without the high markups of processed imported goods. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T006#GNS227_U3_T006_h7)

question: When is a nursing research topic considered to lack practical value?

options.A: If it fails to include at least five different hospitals
options.B: If it uses complex laboratory equipment
options.C: If it fails to change or improve current clinical practice
options.D: If it generates millions of naira in profit

explanation: If the findings don't help us care for patients better at the bedside, the study misses the main point of nursing research. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T4#GNS217_U3_T4_h2)

question: Why is jaundice that appears within the first twenty-four hours of birth considered dangerous?

options.A: It shows that the baby is suffering from severe dehydration
options.B: It indicates that Vitamin K was not given at birth
options.C: It is pathological and points to serious underlying problems
options.D: It means the baby is drinking too much breast milk

explanation: Normal jaundice appears later; jaundice on day one is usually caused by blood group mismatches or severe liver issues needing urgent care. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T51#GNS214_U1_T51_h8)

question: Which phase of the ovarian cycle always stays pretty much the same length for most women?

options.A: Proliferative phase
options.B: Menstrual phase
options.C: Luteal phase
options.D: Follicular phase

explanation: The luteal phase is wonderfully predictable, lasting right around 14 days. It's the follicular phase before it that likes to change length and mix things up! [learn more](GNS121_U5_T4#GNS121_U5_T4_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical outcome of a toxic or poor leadership style in nursing?

options.A: Increased nurse absenteeism
options.B: Communication breakdowns
options.C: Improved patient safety culture
options.D: High staff burnout rates

explanation: Poor leadership damages safety culture rather than improving it, leading to errors and poor teamwork. [learn more](GST321_U3_T3#GST321_U3_T3_h7)

question: Where does personal protective equipment rank in the hierarchy of hazard controls?

options.A: Below administrative controls but above substitution
options.B: At the very bottom as a last resort
options.C: At the very top as the best choice
options.D: Right above elimination

explanation: PPE is the last line of defense because it does not stop the hazard itself, only protects the individual wearing it if other controls fail. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h6)

question: How did nursing education in Nigeria change after the country gained independence in 1960?

options.A: Universities began offering degree programs in nursing science
options.B: Training was moved entirely out of hospitals into military camps
options.C: All foreign-trained nurses were banned from practicing locally
options.D: Traditional herbalism completely replaced western pharmacology

explanation: After independence, nursing grew rapidly as a profession, and Nigerian universities started offering degree courses to elevate nurse training. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h4)

question: Which layer of the skin acts as the anchor, attaching the skin to muscles and bones underneath?

options.A: Papillary dermis
options.B: Hypodermis
options.C: Stratum corneum
options.D: Epidermis

explanation: Spot on! The hypodermis (also called the subcutaneous layer) sits right at the bottom, holding your skin securely to the structures underneath like muscles and bones. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T2#GNS211_U2_T2_h1)

question: What two main things interact during a serological test to confirm a microbe is present?

options.A: Peptidoglycan and crystal violet
options.B: Agar and nutrient broth
options.C: Hydrogen peroxide and catalase
options.D: Antigens and antibodies

explanation: You got it! Serology relies on the precise lock-and-key fit between the germ's antigens and our body's antibodies. [learn more](GST114_U5_T3#GST114_U5_T3_h6)

question: How do Mastomys rats spread the Lassa virus around?

options.A: By biting humans aggressively during daylight hours
options.B: By carrying ticks that drop onto human skin
options.C: By shedding the virus in their urine, faeces, and saliva
options.D: Through respiratory droplets when they sneeze or cough

explanation: Even though the rats don't look sick, their droppings and urine constantly contaminate food items and household surfaces. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T8#GNS214_U1_T8_h2)

question: Which measurement is frequently referred to as the fifth vital sign?

options.A: Weight
options.B: Height
options.C: Urinary output
options.D: Pain

explanation: Pain is routinely assessed alongside traditional vital signs to monitor patient comfort and well-being. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h5)

question: What does the term 'oophoritis' mean?

options.A: Swelling of the fallopian tubes
options.B: Cyst formation on the cervix
options.C: Inflammation of the ovaries
options.D: Infection of the uterine lining

explanation: You've got this! Oophoritis simply means inflammation of one or both ovaries, usually caused by an infection. Great start! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T31#GNS216_U5_T31_h1)

question: Which official body is responsible for regulating nursing education and practice in Nigeria?

options.A: The Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria
options.B: The Federal Ministry of Health
options.C: The West African Health Organization
options.D: The Nigerian Medical Association

explanation: The NMCN is our main governing body! They are legally empowered to control and set the standards for all nursing and midwifery practice across Nigeria. [learn more](GST321_U10_T4#GST321_U10_T4_h2)

question: What is the term used to describe the social, economic, and environmental factors that shape mental wellbeing?

options.A: Clinical diagnostic criteria
options.B: Biological stress markers
options.C: Social determinants of health
options.D: Hereditary personality traits

explanation: Social determinants of health encompass the conditions in which people are born, grow, live, work, and age that heavily influence mental health. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T7#GNS314_U1_T7_h2)

question: Why must nurses watch for child abuse in every family, rich or poor?

options.A: Child maltreatment occurs across all backgrounds regardless of status
options.B: Wealthy families are statistically more prone to emotional abuse
options.C: Lower-income families rarely report physical injuries
options.D: Government policies mandate screening only in high-poverty areas

explanation: Abuse doesn't care about money or social class. Keep an open mind and screen everyone, no matter their background! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T24#GNS225_U5_T24_h1)

question: How do vaccines work to protect a child's body against infections?

options.A: By stimulating the immune system to produce antibodies
options.B: By coating the stomach lining to block germ absorption
options.C: By increasing the body temperature to kill viruses
options.D: By providing immediate chemical destruction of all bacteria

explanation: Exactly! Vaccines introduce safe, weakened parts of a germ to train the immune system so it knows how to fight back if the real disease ever shows up. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T54#GNS214_U1_T54_h4)

question: How does community mobilisation directly support primary health care goals?

options.A: By building large tertiary teaching hospitals in every small town
options.B: By stopping patients from visiting traditional birth attendants
options.C: By helping people manage preventable diseases and improve local sanitation
options.D: By replacing community health workers with paid international staff

explanation: Primary health care focuses on prevention and community-level action, which mobilisation directly achieves. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T1#GNS124_U4_T1_h3)

question: What is the preferred method for first-trimester uterine evacuation in post-abortion care?

options.A: High-dose oral oxytocin alone
options.B: Manual vacuum aspiration
options.C: Sharp metallic curettage without anesthesia
options.D: Major open abdominal surgery

explanation: Well done! Manual vacuum aspiration (MVA) is widely preferred because it is safe, highly effective, and much gentler than older methods. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T006#GNS226_U5_T006_h3)

question: What is the everyday clinical nickname for a bag-valve-mask device?

options.A: Suction catheter
options.B: Venturi mask
options.C: Ambu bag
options.D: Nebulizer

explanation: You will hear nurses and doctors call this the 'Ambu bag' all the time on the ward. It's your best friend in an emergency! [learn more](GNS315_U3_T5#GNS315_U3_T5_h3)

question: Why do nurses keep taking classes and training long after leaving nursing school?

options.A: To replace basic nursing school education completely
options.B: To guarantee an automatic promotion in the hospital
options.C: To fulfill mandatory paperwork for the ministry of health
options.D: To maintain and update professional knowledge and skills

explanation: Medicine and nursing change every day! Continuing education helps us stay sharp, keep our clinical skills fresh, and give our patients the best care possible. You've got this! [learn more](GST321_U8_T8#GST321_U8_T8_h1)

question: Which of these is a very common reason to perform a laparoscopy?

options.A: Extraction of kidney stones
options.B: Drainage of a cerebral abscess
options.C: Repair of a fractured femur bone
options.D: Removal of an inflamed appendix

explanation: Brilliant! Removing an appendix using tiny cuts (laparoscopic appendectomy) is a very common and safe way to treat appendicitis. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T5#GNS221_U2_T5_h2)

question: What is the biggest advantage of having a separate casualty theatre in the hospital?

options.A: It completely removes the need for sterilization protocols
options.B: It reduces the number of doctors required on duty
options.C: It allows student nurses to perform surgeries independently
options.D: It preserves major operating theatres for complex and major surgeries

explanation: You nailed it! Separating minor cases from major ones ensures our heavy-duty ORs are always ready when a major surgical emergency rolls in. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T2#GNS123_U5_T2_h4)

question: Knowing the exact classification and drug-resistance profile of an infecting organism directly helps the nurse do what?

options.A: Determining the patient's expected hospital discharge date
options.B: Administering targeted antimicrobial therapy effectively
options.C: Calculating the patient's exact daily fluid intake
options.D: Choosing the correct hospital room wall paint color

explanation: When you know the exact bug and what drugs it hates, the medical team can prescribe the precise medication to knock it out quickly and safely. [learn more](GST114_U1_T4#GST114_U1_T4_h7)

question: What is the main goal of giving a standard clinical vaccine?

options.A: To provide immediate chemical relief from chronic joint inflammation
options.B: To destroy all existing white blood cells in the patient's body
options.C: To permanently block the liver from metabolizing oral medications
options.D: To introduce safe antigens that stimulate long-term memory cells

explanation: Vaccines give a harmless 'practice preview' of an infection so the immune system can build memory cells and protect the patient later. [learn more](GST114_U4_T2#GST114_U4_T2_h8)

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier stopping women from using post-abortion contraception?

options.A: Fear of unpleasant side effects
options.B: Lack of transport to the clinic
options.C: Guaranteed 100 percent long-term effectiveness
options.D: High product costs at the pharmacy

explanation: High effectiveness is a great thing! Fear, cost, and travel issues are the real hurdles patients face. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T016#GNS226_U5_T016_h6)

question: Why might a patient with a cyst test negative on a routine antibody blood test?

options.A: A thick, intact cyst wall can prevent antigens from triggering a strong immune response
options.B: Human antibodies cannot bind to parasite proteins
options.C: Antibodies only appear after the cyst has completely dissolved
options.D: Blood tests only detect adult tapeworms living in the intestines

explanation: If the outer wall seals the cyst tightly, very little leaks out into the blood to trigger antibodies, leading to false negatives. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T25#GNS313_U2_T25_h6)

question: What are two essential features of a proper sharps disposal container?

options.A: It must be puncture-resistant and leak-proof
options.B: It must be washed and reused between patients
options.C: It must be made of soft, flexible cardboard
options.D: It must be transparent to monitor waste levels

explanation: Sharps containers must be tough enough to stop needles from poking through and solid enough to keep any fluids inside. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T3#GNS122_U3_T3_h7)

question: Which of these is a classic example of a 'human factor' contributing to a mistake during a shift?

options.A: An outdated drug manual printed twenty years ago
options.B: A hospital purchasing cheap intravenous pumps with broken screens
options.C: A nurse calculating a drug dose while distracted by a loud argument
options.D: A severe shortage of nursing staff on a night shift

explanation: Distractions, fatigue, and stress are human factors that mess with our concentration. That's why quiet medication rooms are so important! [learn more](GST319_U5_T2#GST319_U5_T2_h3)

question: Why do nurses check the skin right around a wound (the periwound area), not just the wound itself?

options.A: It determines how much protein the patient needs in their diet.
options.B: It dictates the exact brand of dressing the doctor must prescribe.
options.C: It shows if drainage or moisture is damaging the healthy skin around the wound.
options.D: It helps calculate the exact surface area in square centimeters.

explanation: Spotting issues early around the wound helps you catch irritation or moisture damage before the wound starts getting bigger. You've got this! [learn more](GNS324_U3_T4#GNS324_U3_T4_h1)

question: Which nursing action demonstrates good interpersonal communication during a patient counselling session?

options.A: Telling the patient their cultural beliefs are completely foolish
options.B: Maintaining an open posture and actively listening without judgment
options.C: Interrupting the patient frequently to speed up the consultation
options.D: Looking strictly at the clinic register while the patient speaks

explanation: Empathy and non-judgmental listening make patients feel safe enough to open up and tell you what's really going on. You're developing great clinical bedside manner! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T8#GNS124_U5_T8_h7)

question: A healthy toddler suddenly starts eating less food than before. What is the most likely reason for this?

options.A: Growth velocity naturally slows down after infancy, reducing food demand
options.B: The child is entering a severe phase of permanent nutritional failure
options.C: Breast milk or formula is no longer needed in any form
options.D: The child has developed an irreversible eating disorder

explanation: Don't panic if a toddler's appetite dips! Because growth slows down after year one, they simply don't need as many calories per kilogram. It's completely normal. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T005#GNS227_U2_T005_h3)

question: Why might a nurse practitioner run thyroid blood tests for a patient dealing with sexual dysfunction?

options.A: It is a mandatory legal requirement for pelvic exams
options.B: Thyroid medication cures all forms of orgasmic disorder
options.C: Thyroid glands directly control vaginal lubrication
options.D: Endocrine disorders can alter energy levels and libido

explanation: Makes total sense! Our hormones and metabolism affect our daily energy, mood, and sex drive. Checking the thyroid helps rule out hidden imbalances. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T25#GNS312_U1_T25_h6)

question: Which factor contributes heavily to nursing staff shortages in many Nigerian health units?

options.A: Mandatory retirement at age twenty-five
options.B: The migration of experienced nurses abroad
options.C: Strict laws banning hospital employment
options.D: A complete lack of nursing training schools

explanation: You're spot on. The 'japa' wave has caused many skilled nurses to move abroad for better opportunities, leaving local units short-staffed. [learn more](GST321_U6_T2#GST321_U6_T2_h8)

question: Why is having a personal interest in your research topic important?

options.A: It removes the need for formal ethical approval
options.B: It makes the data analysis process completely automatic
options.C: It gives the researcher motivation to complete the demanding project
options.D: It automatically guarantees funding from the government

explanation: Research writing can get tough! Genuine curiosity and passion for your topic are what keep you going through the late nights. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T4#GNS217_U3_T4_h5)

question: What does the popular '60/60 rule' recommend when using earphones or headphones?

options.A: Listening at no more than sixty percent volume for sixty minutes daily
options.B: Taking a sixty-minute break after every sixty steps taken
options.C: Keeping the device sixty inches away from the ears at all times
options.D: Using headphones for no more than sixty hours a week

explanation: The 60/60 rule is an easy trick to protect your ears from loud music damage. Try keeping your volume at 60% or lower for no more than 60 minutes a day! [learn more](GNS311_U3_T9#GNS311_U3_T9_h2)

question: Why is the elimination of handwritten nursing notes considered a major safety improvement?

options.A: It makes paper storage rooms completely unnecessary in every hospital
options.B: It allows computers to automatically write the discharge summary for the doctor
options.C: It prevents medication errors caused by misreading unclear handwriting
options.D: It ensures that nurses never make any clinical documentation mistakes

explanation: Clear digital text removes the guesswork and dangerous mistakes that frequently arise from reading messy or faded handwriting on paper charts. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h4)

question: Why is it super important to write down a clear methodology in your research?

options.A: To allow other researchers to replicate the study
options.B: To hide any potential errors made during data collection
options.C: To increase the total word count of the document
options.D: To prove that the researcher spent a lot of money

explanation: Good science can be repeated! Clear methods mean other nurses can test the same idea to see if it works for their patients too. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T3#GNS224_U3_T3_h4)

question: What unit of measurement do electronic IV infusion pumps typically use to set fluid rates?

options.A: Liters per 24 hours
options.B: Milliliters per hour
options.C: Drops per second
options.D: Grams per minute

explanation: Infusion pumps are programmed directly in mL/hr to deliver precise fluid volumes over time. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T5#GNS125_U3_T5_h7)

question: How does chloride rushing into brain cells help calm the nervous system?

options.A: It blocks the release of oxygen from nearby red blood cells
options.B: It depolarizes the cell membrane to speed up reflex pathways
options.C: It stops the production of cellular energy molecules in mitochondria
options.D: It hyperpolarizes the cell membrane, making electrical firing less likely

explanation: When negative chloride ions flood the inside of the cell, it becomes 'hyperpolarized'—meaning it's much harder for runaway electrical signals to trigger it. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T1#GNS223_U6_T1_h4)

question: What is the main sign of neurasthenia?

options.A: Chronic nervous exhaustion and physical fatigue
options.B: Permanent neurological nerve damage
options.C: Sudden episodes of complete muscle paralysis
options.D: Severe cognitive decline and memory loss

explanation: You've got this! Neurasthenia is simply known as a condition of ongoing physical tiredness and nervous burnout. Keep up the great work! [learn more](GNS314_U2_T9#GNS314_U2_T9_h1)

question: A nurse researcher splits a hospital's staff into day-shift and night-shift groups, then randomly picks nurses from both. What sampling method is this?

options.A: Snowball sampling
options.B: Quota sampling
options.C: Stratified random sampling
options.D: Convenience sampling

explanation: Brilliant! Dividing people into meaningful groups (strata) like shifts and then picking randomly from each is stratified sampling. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T17#GNS224_U1_T17_h4)

question: What is an example of secondary epidemiologic data?

options.A: Measuring the mid-upper arm circumference of children
options.B: Interviewing village elders about local health beliefs
options.C: Conducting blood pressure checks at a local market square
options.D: Reviewing past mortality records from the health ministry

explanation: Secondary data refers to information that was already gathered by other agencies or researchers in the past. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T1#GNS313_U4_T1_h2)

question: What is the primary goal of food purchasing in nutritional care?

options.A: Minimizing the time spent on meal preparation
options.B: Reducing the variety of meals served daily
options.C: Buying the most expensive ingredients available
options.D: Ensuring access to safe and nutrient-dense foods

explanation: Food purchasing aims to acquire safe, wholesome ingredients that supply the necessary nutrients for good health. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T006#GNS227_U3_T006_h1)

question: What is a fomite in the context of infection control?

options.A: A specialized mask used for airborne disease isolation
options.B: A living insect that carries parasites to humans
options.C: An inanimate object that can transmit infectious agents
options.D: A chemical spray used to clean hospital floors

explanation: Fomites are non-living surfaces or objects like stethoscopes or tables that hold onto germs and pass them along. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T81#GNS214_U1_T81_h3)

question: If a partner stops you from working and controls all the money in the house, what kind of abuse is that?

options.A: Emotional abuse
options.B: Economic abuse
options.C: Sexual abuse
options.D: Physical abuse

explanation: Correct! Economic abuse happens when someone cuts off another person's access to money or financial independence to trap them. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T23#GNS225_U5_T23_h2)

question: What is the main job of sensory nerves in our body?

options.A: Producing hormones to regulate metabolic rate
options.B: Transmitting information from body tissues to the central nervous system
options.C: Carrying signals away from the brain to muscles
options.D: Controlling involuntary heart contractions

explanation: Spot on! Sensory nerves act like telephone wires, carrying messages from your skin and organs back to the brain and spinal cord so you know what's happening around you. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T28#GNS211_U3_T28_h1)

question: How do patriarchal family structures often impact women's reproductive health in Nigeria?

options.A: They eliminate all cultural barriers to hospital delivery
options.B: They require husbands to attend all antenatal checkups
options.C: They often restrict women's autonomy in making healthcare decisions
options.D: They automatically grant women full control over household finances

explanation: In homes where men hold all the decision-making power, a woman may need her husband's permission or money just to visit a clinic, which can dangerously delay her care. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T4#GNS216_U1_T4_h6)

question: What is the main financial goal of the Drug Revolving Fund (DRF) model?

options.A: Providing all medications completely free of charge
options.B: Subsidizing staff salaries within the facility
options.C: Generating massive profits for the hospital
options.D: Cost-recovery and replacement of stock

explanation: You've got this! Think of a DRF as a self-sustaining cycle: money from selling drugs is used straight away to buy fresh stock, so the clinic never runs out or needs emergency government bailouts. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T5#GNS215_U3_T5_h1)

question: A disaster survivor visits the clinic three months after a flood complaining of sudden nightmares, severe jumpiness, and avoiding the riverbank entirely. What condition is most likely?

options.A: Normal adjustment reaction
options.B: Bipolar manic episode
options.C: Acute Stress Disorder
options.D: Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder

explanation: Flashbacks, avoidance, and hyperarousal lasting months after the traumatic event point directly toward PTSD. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T6#GNS315_U5_T6_h3)

question: Why is observing a client in their home better than only seeing them in a clinic?

options.A: It reveals daily coping habits and environmental triggers
options.B: It replaces the need for any future medical doctor consultations
options.C: It removes all symptoms of mental illness permanently
options.D: It guarantees the client will take all their prescribed drugs

explanation: Being in the home gives nurses a realistic view of daily life, family stress, and living conditions that a clinic setting hides. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T6#GNS314_U4_T6_h1)

question: Which type of adverse event involves a patient picking up a brand new infection while admitted to the hospital?

question: Which of these is a big legal no-no when writing nursing notes?

question: How do sheltered workshops differ from regular commercial workplaces?

question: What crucial information must you always write down in a patient's referral note?

question: What is the main difference between HIV and AIDS?

question: Why should you as a nurse always ask your patients if they use traditional herbs or local remedies?

question: Which group often faces sudden income drops during tough economic times due to a lack of job security?

question: A nurse checks a patient's skin, hair, and oral mucosa for signs of vitamin deficiencies. Which part of the ABCD framework is this?

question: Which accessory gland makes the biggest chunk of the fluid found in semen?

question: When counseling a new mother on her diet, what is an important duty for you as a nurse?

options.C: Requiring the mother to purchase expensive foreign supplements

question: How does passive surveillance generally collect its data?

options.A: Patients fill out online surveys from home
options.B: Clinics and labs send reports without being prompted
options.C: Health workers actively search hospital wards for cases

question: Who is widely recognized as America's first trained psychiatric nurse?

question: What does 'unity of command' mean during a disaster response?

options.A: Private businesses take full financial control of public hospitals

question: What is the primary focus of community mobilisation for mental health?

options.A: Collective action to improve psychological well-being

question: When smooth muscles in the penis relax, what happens to the helical arteries?

options.C: They collapse entirely to prevent any further fluid entry

question: Why do we need to eat water-soluble vitamins more often than fat-soluble ones?

question: What is the primary medication administered immediately after birth to prevent postpartum hemorrhage?

question: Why are babies and young children extra vulnerable to the risks of self-medication?

options.D: They have higher blood volume than healthy adults

question: What simple tool do nurses use to plot a child's weight against their age during clinic visits?

question: How do alcohol-based disinfectants actually kill germs?

options.A: Forming hard crystals inside the bacterial nucleus
options.B: Blocking the respiratory system of the patient

options.D: Lowering the room temperature to freeze pathogens

question: What do we mainly mean by 'sewage' in public health?

options.C: Industrial runoff containing only chemical fertilizers
options.D: Rainwater collected exclusively from street gutters

question: How do the ureters move urine down from the kidneys into the bladder?

options.C: By passive diffusion through tiny microscopic pores
options.D: By rhythmic muscular contractions known as peristalsis

question: Why should a nurse give written discharge instructions about pain meds to a recovering patient?

question: What is a major drawback of rapid bolus tube feedings?

question: How many copies of a mutated gene must a child inherit to show symptoms of an autosomal recessive condition?

question: What type of lab growth media has extra nutrients to help delicate, picky bacteria grow?

question: A patient has swollen ankles, bulging neck veins, and crackles in the lungs. What do these signs point to?

question: Why do teenagers sometimes make impulsive choices or take big risks?

question: Why does severe anaemia put a mother at high risk for heavy bleeding after delivery (postpartum hemorrhage)?

question: Which hormone does the body pump out in large amounts during long periods of stress?

question: What does 'leadership disconnect' mean in healthcare management?

question: Which of these research questions is best answered with a quantitative design?

question: Which of these is a major reason for internal displacement, especially in Northern Nigeria?

question: A patient taking a new antiarrhythmic drug tells the nurse they feel dizzy and lightheaded. What is the best initial nursing action?

question: Which specialist checks if a patient can swallow safely and recommends the right food textures?

question: Why is it smart for a nurse manager to catch early warning signs instead of waiting for a big formal complaint?

question: Why should you test a new idea on a small scale before launching it across the whole hospital?

question: High blood pressure, protein in the urine, and sudden swelling during pregnancy are classic warning signs of:

question: How do nursing leaders make sure a successful new practice becomes permanent?

question: What is the biggest health benefit of colostrum (the first breastmilk)?

question: If a data point on a control chart suddenly shoots way past the upper limit, what should the nursing team do?

question: Why is supportive nursing care more common than using specific antidotes for poisoned patients?

question: Why must men with an enlarged prostate be very careful with central anticholinergics?

question: A patient with severe cholera is passing profuse watery stool. Which primary supportive nursing intervention takes priority?

question: How do long-acting injectable antipsychotics make community care easier?

question: What is a must-have when introducing a complex new clinical workflow?

question: A healthy adult client closes their eyes and relaxes quietly. Which brain wave pattern is most likely to become dominant?

question: How do RFID tags help clinical staff manage equipment?

question: What does healthcare outsourcing actually mean?

question: Standard precautions apply to which of these body fluids in the ward?

question: Why are routine screenings, like annual tuberculosis tests, so important for hospital staff?

question: Why do nurses monitor blood inflammatory markers like ESR and CRP in osteomyelitis patients?

question: Why can an overweight patient still suffer from malnutrition?

question: What do altmetrics mainly track when measuring how far a research study has traveled?

question: Which hormone is primarily responsible for the actual production of milk in the alveoli?

question: Why do perpetrators usually carry out breast ironing?

question: What is a common pitfall parents fall into when a toddler's appetite drops?

question: Which system in the body pumps out stress hormones like cortisol and adrenaline when you face a sudden scare?

explanation: Amiodarone is a broad-spectrum drug that blocks sodium, potassium, and calcium channels while also acting as a beta-blocker. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T3#GNS223_U1_T3_h5)

question: Why should a nurse advise a patient never to stop psychiatric medication abruptly?

options.A: The patient will instantly lose all their memories
options.B: It is against hospital administrative policy to miss one dose
options.C: Doctors will refuse to see the patient ever again
options.D: Sudden discontinuation can trigger severe withdrawal or quick relapse

explanation: Abruptly stopping psychotropic drugs often causes a sudden return of acute symptoms or dangerous physical withdrawal effects. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h5)

question: A nurse classifies patient satisfaction scores as 'poor', 'fair', or 'good'. Which level of measurement is this?

options.A: Nominal
options.B: Ordinal
options.C: Ratio
options.D: Interval

explanation: Satisfaction grades have a logical order from poor to good, making them ordinal data, though the distance between the grades is not mathematically fixed. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T1#GNS224_U2_T1_h3)

question: Which of these is a key part of our fast-acting, innate immunity?

options.A: Phagocytosis by macrophages
options.B: Production of specific antibodies
options.C: Long-term memory cell creation
options.D: Delayed T-lymphocyte activation

explanation: Macrophages are like the body's cleanup crew. They use phagocytosis (swallowing up germs) as a quick, first-line defense against any invader. [learn more](GST114_U4_T6#GST114_U4_T6_h2)

question: A patient with a joint contracture has a permanent limitation in movement. What causes this change?

options.A: Shortening and tightening of surrounding connective tissues
options.B: A sudden increase in joint fluid volume
options.C: Complete melting of the cartilage inside the joint capsule
options.D: Overgrowth of the bone ends inside the joint

explanation: Great thinking! When joints aren't moved regularly, nearby tissues like tendons and ligaments tighten up and shorten, leading to a contracture. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T1#GNS221_U1_T1_h2)

question: If you want to see how a family interacts with external community systems like schools and churches, which tool should you use?

options.A: Temperature graph
options.B: Eco-map
options.C: Growth chart
options.D: Genogram

explanation: An eco-map shows connections between family members and outside social structures, highlighting where they get support or stress. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T3#GNS124_U2_T3_h5)

question: A child swallowed a brightly colored liquid from a soft drink bottle. What is the nurse's most important first step?

options.A: Place the child flat on their back to rest quietly
options.B: Induce vomiting immediately to remove the liquid
options.C: Identify the exact substance swallowed without delaying care
options.D: Administer large amounts of palm oil to neutralize the poison

explanation: Knowing the exact poison helps the doctor give the right treatment. Never force vomiting for chemicals, as it can cause worse burns on the way back up! [learn more](GNS315_U2_T3#GNS315_U2_T3_h3)

question: A patient with a challenging personality tries to manipulate the nursing staff by asking different nurses for special rules. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Ignore the patient completely and refuse to answer any of their call lights
options.B: Scold the patient publicly so they feel embarrassed and stop asking
options.C: Let the patient break the rules to keep them happy and prevent arguments
options.D: Ensure all staff members consistently communicate and enforce the same unit boundaries

explanation: Consistency among all staff members prevents manipulation and helps patients learn reliable, healthy boundaries. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T8#GNS314_U1_T8_h6)

question: Which common blood test checks for both anemia and signs of infection?

options.A: Blood Glucose Test
options.B: Complete Blood Count
options.C: Urinalysis
options.D: Malaria Parasite Test

explanation: A Complete Blood Count (CBC) looks at your red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets. It is super helpful for spotting anemia and infections! Keep it up. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T4#GNS124_U6_T4_h3)

question: Why do disaster coordinators try to house elderly or chronically ill patients close to the main medical tents?

options.A: To isolate them completely from the rest of the community
options.B: To allow for quicker response if their health condition suddenly deteriorates
options.C: To make it easier for them to clean the medical equipment
options.D: To reduce the walking distance for medical staff delivering food

explanation: Vulnerable patients can crash quickly in emergencies. Keeping them close to medical help means doctors and nurses can reach them in seconds. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T5#GNS315_U5_T5_h8)

question: Why must used needles and razor blades go straight into a puncture-proof sharps box?

options.A: To comply with waste disposal rules without needing to wash them first
options.B: To ensure that they can be easily sharpened and reused for the next patient
options.C: To keep the delivery tray looking neat and tidy during the procedure
options.D: To prevent accidental needle-stick injuries and bloodborne pathogen transmission

explanation: Sharps safety keeps everyone safe! Dropping them right in the box protects you, your colleagues, and waste handlers from nasty infections like HIV or hepatitis. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T008#GNS226_U3_T008_h7)

question: Besides sharing new rules, what must effective communication include during a healthcare transition?

options.A: An explanation of why the change improves patient outcomes
options.B: Strict orders that forbid nurses from asking questions
options.C: Detailed financial records of the hospital budget
options.D: Immediate disciplinary threats for non-compliant staff members

explanation: When nurses see the 'why'—especially how it helps patients—they are much more willing to get on board. [learn more](GST319_U2_T5#GST319_U2_T5_h5)

question: What happens when a community actively participates in planning its own local health programs?

options.A: The programs are more likely to succeed and last long-term
options.B: Western medicine is completely rejected by the villagers
options.C: The government stops funding public health services entirely
options.D: Nurses no longer need to work in rural health centers

explanation: When people help build a program, they take ownership of it, making it much more sustainable over time. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h4)

question: What is the first step evaluated during the primary survey of an emergency patient?

options.A: Circulation
options.B: Breathing
options.C: Airway
options.D: Disability

explanation: The primary survey strictly follows the ABCDE mnemonic, placing airway assessment and management at the very top. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T1#GNS315_U1_T1_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a valid reason for providing proper citations in a literature review?

options.A: To avoid academic dishonesty and professional plagiarism charges
options.B: To give proper intellectual credit to the original researchers
options.C: To allow readers to verify the accuracy of your clinical claims
options.D: To make your reference list look as long and intimidating as possible

explanation: We use citations to give credit and let others check our facts—never just to pad the length of our bibliography! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T5#GNS217_U3_T5_h8)

question: Why do Registered Nurses rely so much on updates from nursing assistants?

options.A: Assistants spend the most direct time observing daily changes
options.B: RNs are not permitted to enter patient rooms independently
options.C: Assistants are legally required to sign off on drug charts
options.D: Hospital policies mandate daily verbal briefings from staff

explanation: Because nursing assistants spend the most time helping with everyday tasks, they are often the first ones to notice tiny shifts in how a patient is feeling. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T7#GNS321_U3_T7_h2)

question: How does the endocrine system's signaling mainly differ from the nervous system?

options.A: Nervous signaling relies entirely on blood transport systems
options.B: Endocrine signaling uses fast electrical impulses directly to tissues
options.C: Nervous signaling controls long-term growth instead of rapid reflexes
options.D: Endocrine signaling is slower and provides longer-lasting control

explanation: While nerves give quick, snap reactions (like pulling your hand from fire), hormones take a bit longer to travel through the blood, but their effects stick around much longer. Great to know for clinical practice! [learn more](GNS211_U1_T10#GNS211_U1_T10_h1)

question: What does 'stock strength' mean when you look at a medicine label?

options.A: The amount of active drug in a specific unit of volume or weight
options.B: The expiration date of the manufactured pharmaceutical product
options.C: The maximum safe dose a human body can tolerate in a day
options.D: The total number of pills left inside the medicine bottle

explanation: Spot on! Stock strength simply tells you how concentrated the drug is in the package you're holding. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T6#GNS125_U2_T6_h3)

question: How does a respiratory virus normally leave the body?

options.A: Urine output
options.B: Coughing and sneezing
options.C: Intact skin surface
options.D: Sweat glands

explanation: Exactly! Respiratory germs love to catch a ride on droplets expelled through the nose and mouth when someone coughs or sneezes. [learn more](GST114_U2_T1#GST114_U2_T1_h4)

question: How do nurses use triage during a mass casualty incident?

options.A: By treating patients strictly on a first-come, first-served basis
options.B: By waiting for international doctors to arrive before touching any patient
options.C: By focusing only on patients who show no signs of physical injury
options.D: By sorting patients based on the urgency of their medical needs and survival chance

explanation: Exactly! Triage helps nurses quickly prioritize care so that the most critical patients get help first. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T12#GNS315_U1_T12_h5)

question: Why is post-abortion care viewed as a complete package rather than just a single medical procedure?

options.A: It must involve legal teams alongside medical doctors in every case
options.B: It requires multiple surgical operations over a span of several months
options.C: It combines emergency treatment, counseling, contraception, and health linkages
options.D: It is only performed in specialized tertiary teaching hospitals

explanation: Spot on! PAC covers more than just the immediate physical cleanup—it looks at the whole person by offering counseling, family planning, and follow-up support. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T006#GNS226_U5_T006_h1)

question: Why does kidney compensation take longer than lung compensation during an acid-base imbalance?

options.A: Kidneys must slowly adjust tubular secretion and bicarbonate synthesis over days
options.B: Renal blood flow is too slow to deliver chemical messages effectively
options.C: Kidneys only operate when the patient is asleep and resting
options.D: Metabolic acids take longer to dissolve in plasma than dissolved gases

explanation: The lungs can change your breathing rate in seconds, but the kidneys need hours to days to manufacture new bicarbonate and adjust what they filter out. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T13#GNS121_U2_T13_h5)

question: Why do we treat broken glass ampoules with the same care as needles?

options.A: They dissolve quickly inside standard trash bins
options.B: They are made from recycled hospital plastics
options.C: They contain live viral vaccines inside them
options.D: They can easily puncture skin and cause deep cuts

explanation: Any broken glass with a sharp edge can cut you and introduce nasty germs. Treat them like needles! [learn more](GST114_U2_T8#GST114_U2_T8_h2)

question: Which blood tests are most commonly used to evaluate kidney filtration function?

options.A: Serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen
options.B: White blood cell count and hemoglobin
options.C: Serum electrolytes and platelet count
options.D: Prothrombin time and international normalized ratio

explanation: Creatinine and blood urea nitrogen are waste products filtered by the kidneys, making them reliable indicators of renal function. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T2#GNS213_U4_T2_h4)

question: Which muscle groups need the most strengthening when a patient is learning to use crutches after an amputation?

options.A: Facial and neck muscles
options.B: Small toe flexors
options.C: Lower leg calf muscles
options.D: Upper body and core muscles

explanation: Using crutches without a lower limb means the arms, shoulders, and chest have to do all the heavy lifting. Time for some push-ups! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T12#GNS324_U4_T12_h6)

question: What is the primary danger of leaving a needle stuck in a multidose vaccine vial?

options.A: It changes the recommended dosage for pediatric clients
options.B: It provides an easy entry route for environmental bacteria
options.C: It causes the liquid vaccine to freeze too quickly
options.D: It increases the expiration date printed on the label

explanation: Leaving a needle in the stopper breaks the closed seal of the vial, allowing airborne or contact germs to contaminate the remaining doses inside. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h3)

question: Where is laboratory research typically carried out?

options.A: In busy hospital waiting rooms
options.B: During community health outreach
options.C: Inside patients' private homes
options.D: In a controlled, artificial setting

explanation: Correct! Lab research takes place in controlled environments where scientists can carefully manage and manipulate variables. [learn more](GNS217_U1_T4#GNS217_U1_T4_h5)

question: What type of information belongs in a standard incident report?

options.A: Derogatory remarks about an uncooperative patient
options.B: Personal opinions on which doctor or nurse caused the problem
options.C: Detailed theories on how much money the hospital might lose
options.D: Objective facts about what happened and actions taken

explanation: Correct! Incident reports need pure, unbiased facts—just the plain truth of what happened and what care was given right away. [learn more](GST319_U4_T9#GST319_U4_T9_h4)

question: How do rigid hierarchies in some healthcare settings hurt patient safety?

options.A: Patients receive conflicting instructions from different specialists
options.B: Junior nurses may be afraid to speak up or question unsafe orders from senior staff
options.C: Hospital management is unable to purchase necessary medications
options.D: Doctors are forced to perform routine nursing documentation tasks

explanation: Fear of senior staff can keep junior nurses quiet about dangerous orders. Open teamwork saves lives! [learn more](GST319_U6_T5#GST319_U6_T5_h7)

question: A patient admits they smoke too much, but they have zero plans to quit anytime soon. Which stage of change are they in?

options.A: Preparation
options.B: Maintenance
options.C: Precontemplation
options.D: Contemplation

explanation: In precontemplation, a person isn't ready to change yet and might not even see a problem with their habit. It's our job as nurses to meet them where they are with patience! [learn more](GNS225_U2_T27#GNS225_U2_T27_h2)

question: Which social factor is consistently proven to help young girls delay marriage and early childbearing?

options.A: Traditional community ceremonies
options.B: Living in an urban city center
options.C: Access to formal education
options.D: Employment in the agricultural sector

explanation: Education is a powerful tool! When girls stay in school, they gain knowledge, open up better life opportunities, and naturally delay marriage and childbearing. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T1#GNS216_U1_T1_h5)

question: How does partnering with schools help improve childhood immunization rates?

options.A: It forces teachers to administer complex injectable vaccines
options.B: It allows health workers to check vaccination cards and catch up on missed doses
options.C: It ensures that children never catch common colds at home
options.D: It replaces the need for infant clinics at primary health centers

explanation: Schools provide a structured setting where health workers can easily review children's immunization records and administer catch-up vaccines. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T71#GNS214_U1_T71_h7)

question: Why would a nurse need to provide alternative ways for a patient to pass urine or stool?

options.A: The patient is unable to walk to the toilet independently
options.B: The hospital policy requires all bedridden patients to use bedpans
options.C: It reduces the total amount of daily nursing documentation
options.D: It completely prevents any risk of a hospital-acquired infection

explanation: You've got this! We bring in things like bedpans or urinals mainly when a patient is too weak or restricted to safely make it to the bathroom on their own. Simple and practical! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T8#GNS112_U5_T8_h1)

question: Why is it so important to follow a specific journal's instructions before submitting your paper?

options.A: It eliminates any need to report study limitations in the discussion
options.B: It guarantees that the journal will publish the paper without peer review
options.C: It prevents immediate rejection due to formatting or scope mismatches
options.D: It reduces the total word count of the study to under fifty words

explanation: Right! Journals get tons of papers and will often reject them instantly if they don't follow basic formatting and topic guidelines. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T1#GNS224_U4_T1_h4)

question: Why do electronic health record systems keep background 'audit trails' of every click?

options.A: They calculate the total financial cost of hospital supplies used
options.B: They automatically archive old paper records in the basement
options.C: They track every user action in a chart to enforce privacy and accountability
options.D: They measure how fast nurses complete their shift documentation

explanation: Well done! Audit trails quietly record who opened or edited a file. It keeps everyone accountable and stops unauthorized snooping into patient records. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T3#GNS113_U1_T3_h6)

question: Which of these is a misuse of a theoretical framework in a research project?

options.A: Aligning its core concepts with the research questions
options.B: Returning to it during the discussion section to interpret results
options.C: Mentioning it briefly in the introduction and ignoring it for the rest of the study
options.D: Using it to guide the selection of variables and measurement tools

explanation: Correct! Dropping a theory's name in the intro and never using it again leaves your study feeling disconnected and weak. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T12#GNS217_U3_T12_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of bowel preparation before rectovaginal fistula surgery?

options.A: To reduce fecal load and minimize infection risk
options.B: To increase blood pressure during the operation
options.C: To stretch the vaginal walls for easier access
options.D: To test the kidneys for dye clearance

explanation: Clearing the bowel reduces stool contamination at the surgical site, lowering the risk of postoperative wound infection and failure. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h6)

question: What is an important job for nurse managers who deal with financial data?

options.A: Approving pharmaceutical manufacturing licenses
options.B: Fixing broken hospital electrical wiring
options.C: Defending staffing levels and resource needs
options.D: Auditing national tax collection records

explanation: Having good cost data lets nurse managers confidently fight for enough staff and supplies to keep patients safe. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h8)

question: What is the standard recommended temperature range for storing most routine vaccines in a cold chain?

options.A: Between -10°C and -20°C
options.B: Between +30°C and +40°C
options.C: Between +2°C and +8°C
options.D: Between +15°C and +25°C

explanation: Most routine vaccines lose their potency if allowed to freeze or get too warm, requiring a steady storage range of +2°C to +8°C. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T8#GNS313_U1_T8_h7)

question: What should you check or do first when a patient is brought in with a suspected poisoning?

options.A: Drawing blood for toxicology screening
options.B: Identifying the specific poison
options.C: Administering activated charcoal immediately
options.D: Stabilizing the airway, breathing, and circulation

explanation: Great nursing rule to keep in mind! ABC comes before anything else in an emergency. We have to make sure our patient is breathing and has a steady heartbeat before we worry about testing or finding out what they swallowed. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T6#GNS215_U5_T6_h1)

question: What does accountability mean when a registered nurse delegates a task?

options.A: The nursing assistant takes all legal blame if something goes wrong
options.B: The registered nurse remains ultimately responsible for the patient outcome
options.C: Nobody is responsible once the task is handed over to staff
options.D: The hospital management assumes all blame for delegation errors

explanation: While responsibility for doing the task is transferred, the registered nurse retains final accountability for supervising and ensuring patient safety. [learn more](GST321_U1_T13#GST321_U1_T13_h6)

question: Why do large arteries possess thick walls rich in elastic tissue?

options.A: To allow rapid diffusion of oxygen and carbon dioxide across the vessel wall
options.B: To store extra white blood cells during a systemic bacterial infection
options.C: To trap blood clots before they reach smaller vessels in the brain
options.D: To withstand and buffer the high-pressure surges of blood coming directly from the heart

explanation: The high elasticity of large arteries helps them absorb the forceful pulses of blood pumped by the heart, smoothing out pressure fluctuations. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T5#GNS111_U2_T5_h2)

question: If a neighborhood near a busy road and a power plant has high levels of toxic gases, where are those gases mainly coming from?

options.A: Agricultural crop dusting and livestock farming
options.B: Indoor cooking using traditional firewood stoves
options.C: Industrial emissions and vehicular exhaust
options.D: Natural evaporation of stagnant surface water

explanation: Exactly! Power plants pump out industrial emissions, while cars and trucks release vehicle exhaust. Simple as that! [learn more](GST114_U6_T7#GST114_U6_T7_h2)

question: What is the best tool to use for smoothing out rough nail edges after clipping?

options.A: A sharp surgical scissor
options.B: A metal cuticle pusher
options.C: A stiff plastic brush
options.D: An emery board or nail file

explanation: Correct! A nail file or emery board gently buffs away sharp, jagged edges without splitting the nail plate. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T4#GNS112_U5_T4_h4)

question: Why is it clinically important to treat pain quickly in emergency care, beyond just making the patient comfortable?

options.A: It guarantees the patient will be discharged within two hours.
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for any surgical interventions.
options.C: It prevents harmful physiological stress responses like high blood pressure and rapid heart rate.
options.D: It stops all forms of internal bleeding instantly.

explanation: Exactly! Unmanaged pain sends the body into a stress overdrive, pushing up heart rate and blood pressure, which makes stabilizing an emergency patient much harder. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T2#GNS315_U1_T2_h3)

question: Which branch of the Red Cross family focuses specifically on helping people affected by wars and armed conflicts?

options.A: International Federation of Red Cross Societies (IFRC)
options.B: International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC)
options.C: Local National Societies
options.D: World Health Organization (WHO)

explanation: You got it! The ICRC has a special mission under international law to protect and care for victims of war and armed conflict. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T10#GNS315_U1_T10_h4)

question: Which kitchen tool is notorious for trapping wheat crumbs and causing cross-contamination?

options.A: Stainless steel pots used for boiling water
options.B: Toasters used for regular wheat bread
options.C: Ceramic dinner plates washed in hot water
options.D: Glass storage bowls with tight plastic lids

explanation: Toasters hold onto bread crumbs inside their heating coils, making them nearly impossible to clean completely for someone with celiac disease. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T011#GNS227_U6_T011_h6)

question: Why do nurses sometimes hesitate to ask patients about their spiritual needs?

options.A: Lack of available paperwork charts in the nursing station
options.B: Patients always refuse to answer questions about faith
options.C: Fear of imposing personal values or causing offense
options.D: Strict hospital policies forbidding any talk of religion

explanation: It's totally normal to worry about crossing boundaries, but being gentle and respectful makes spiritual care safe and meaningful for the patient. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T13#GNS225_U5_T13_h4)

question: How is a true drug allergy different from a general adverse drug reaction (ADR)?

options.A: ADRs only affect the skin, whereas allergies affect internal organs.
options.B: ADRs are predictable, but allergies are completely impossible to track.
options.C: Allergies involve the immune system, while ADRs can happen through other body processes.
options.D: Allergies always require surgery, while ADRs never do.

explanation: Think of it this way: all allergies are a type of ADR, but allergies specifically trigger your immune system, while other ADRs can happen through normal body chemistry. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T8#GNS125_U5_T8_h1)

question: Which macronutrient provides the highest amount of energy per gram?

options.A: Carbohydrate
options.B: Protein
options.C: Fat
options.D: Water

explanation: Fats provide nine calories per gram, which is more than double the energy density found in carbohydrates or proteins. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T009#GNS227_U6_T009_h3)

question: Roughly how long is a typical research report abstract?

options.A: 10 to 50 words
options.B: Exactly 5,000 words
options.C: 500 to 1,000 words
options.D: 150 to 250 words

explanation: An abstract is a short, sweet summary—usually just a couple of hundred words to give readers a quick preview. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T17#GNS217_U3_T17_h3)

question: Which muscle group is primarily activated by the femoral nerve?

options.A: Quadriceps femoris
options.B: Gastrocnemius
options.C: Gluteus maximus
options.D: Hamstrings

explanation: The femoral nerve innervates the quadriceps muscles on the front of the thigh, which are responsible for straightening the knee. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T26#GNS211_U3_T26_h7)

question: Which of these is a common task for a nurse when dealing with patient insurance?

options.A: Checking patient insurance status and benefit eligibility
options.B: Auditing the financial profits of private hospitals
options.C: Setting the monthly premium rates for insurance companies
options.D: Designing government tax policies for healthcare funding

explanation: You got it! Nurses often check a patient's coverage to make sure treatments are approved and covered by their health scheme. [learn more](GST322_U4_T7#GST322_U4_T7_h6)

question: What is the name of the special, yellowish first milk produced right after birth?

options.A: Lochia
options.B: Meconium
options.C: Serum
options.D: Colostrum

explanation: You got it! Colostrum is nature's gold for the baby—packed with antibodies and protein to protect the newborn and kickstart their digestion. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T013#GNS226_U3_T013_h5)

question: What is the primary male surgical sterilization procedure called?

options.A: Tubal ligation
options.B: Vasectomy
options.C: Orchiectomy
options.D: Prostatectomy

explanation: A vasectomy blocks or cuts the vas deferens tubes to prevent sperm from entering the semen. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T1#GNS225_U3_T1_h4)

question: What is the job of the obturator when putting in a tracheostomy tube?

options.A: To connect the tube directly to the oxygen tubing
options.B: To catch dried mucus inside the main shaft
options.C: To inflate the internal balloon and seal the airway
options.D: To guide the outer cannula smoothly through the stoma

explanation: The obturator has a smooth, rounded tip. It slips inside the tube to make sure the edges don't scratch or damage the tissue when you guide it in. Smooth and safe! [learn more](GNS315_U4_T1#GNS315_U4_T1_h3)

question: When would a nurse researcher choose a qualitative design?

options.A: To test a specific drug dosage on a group of people
options.B: To prove cause and effect using large numerical samples
options.C: To quickly measure blood pressure across a large population
options.D: To explore the emotional details of a patient's illness

explanation: Great thinking! We use qualitative designs when we want rich, descriptive stories about human experiences instead of cold numbers. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T5#GNS224_U1_T5_h1)

question: In cervical cell changes, what makes CIN 3 more serious than the earlier stages?

options.C: Invasion through the basement membrane has already occurred
options.D: Severe dysplasia spans almost the entire thickness of the epithelium

question: Which theorist developed the system of psychoanalysis?

options.A: Ivan Pavlov
options.B: B.F. Skinner
options.C: Sigmund Freud
options.D: Carl Rogers

explanation: Sigmund Freud created psychoanalysis, focusing on the unconscious mind and early childhood experiences. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T3#GNS314_U1_T3_h4)

question: Which of these is a major barrier to nursing research in busy hospitals?

options.A: Excessive amounts of free time during shifts
options.B: Too many available financial grants and computers
options.C: Heavy clinical workloads and staffing shortages
options.D: Strict bans on publishing local healthcare data

explanation: Spot on! When nurse-to-patient ratios are high and everyone is exhausted, it's really tough to find the energy or time for research. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T5#GNS217_U2_T5_h5)

question: Which stomach cells are responsible for secreting hydrochloric acid?

options.A: G-cells
options.B: Goblet cells
